name: zero_width_only_text
why_it_might_slip_through: U+200B is not whitespace to str.strip(), so the empty-text check passes and a blank-looking string reaches the tokenizer.

name: invisible_filler_chars
why_it_might_slip_through: Hangul filler, braille blank and word joiner render as blank but are not stripped by str.strip().

name: control_chars_and_ansi
why_it_might_slip_through: NUL, BEL and an ANSI escape sequence around a real word: text is non-empty, and the raw bytes get written to the audit log.

name: lone_surrogate_escape
why_it_might_slip_through: JSON allows \ud83d alone. Python parses it into an unencodable str; the tokenizer or the UTF-8 audit log write may raise, giving a 500.

name: misnamed_topic_key
why_it_might_slip_through: Valid text plus 'input_topic' (the name used in the log) instead of 'topic'. Pydantic ignores unknown fields, so the topic is silently dropped and the request is treated as topic-less.

name: duplicate_text_key
why_it_might_slip_through: Duplicate keys are legal to the JSON parser; the last 'text' wins, so the whitespace-only first value is never validated.

name: oversized_text_60k_chars
why_it_might_slip_through: No length cap. The tokenizer truncates to 256 tokens only after the whole string is received, tokenized and logged in full.
